title: Jensen Huang’s Next Move? Inside the $50 Billion Chip Startup Rumor
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has set off speculation about what the company’s co-founder might do next. One scenario circulating on social media is that he could raise $50 billion to launch a semiconductor company. The figure traces back to a podcast prediction, and there is no public evidence that Huang has begun fundraising or secured commitments from investors.

Rohan Goswami, a Semafor business reporter, floated the idea on the Prof G Markets podcast during a discussion about whether Huang might return to Nvidia. He suggested that Huang could tap friends and allies to finance a new chip venture. As the idea spread online, some posts described the hypothetical fundraising round as something Huang was already considering.

Nvidia announced Huang’s resignation on November 12 and named longtime finance chief Colette Kress interim chief executive. Kress is retaining her role as chief financial officer while the board searches for a permanent successor. Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and led it for roughly three decades, has said he would be honored to return. Reuters reported that the board was not considering his return.

A new chip company led by Huang would draw attention because of the business he built at Nvidia. Competing in AI hardware would mean recruiting experienced engineers, securing manufacturing capacity and persuading customers to test unfamiliar chips. A challenger would also need software that lets developers run existing workloads without extensive rewrites. Nvidia itself has emphasized how closely it develops its chips, networking and software together.

The shape of any venture would depend on where Huang chose to compete. A company focused on a specific kind of AI workload would face different costs from one trying to build an entire computing platform. For now, Huang has announced neither a company nor a fundraising target. The $50 billion figure remains a prediction about what he might do next.

Prof G Markets, November 17 — The podcast episode where Semafor reporter Rohan Goswami floated the idea of Huang raising $50 billion for a chip startup.
FourWeekMBA, November 20 — Traces the viral claim to Goswami’s prediction. The $50 billion figure remains speculative.
Nvidia’s CEO transition announcement, November 12 and SEC filing — Confirm Huang’s resignation and Colette Kress’s appointment as interim CEO.
Reuters, November 17 — Reports that Huang said he would be honored to return and that Nvidia’s board was not considering his return.
